english.html: larly because, although the difference laid down by our laws, as to the imposition of penalties, between nobles and those of low condition <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup> is not strictly kept in France, where that general rule is held more tenaciously, that crimes and misdeeds cast off and annul all dignity and all privileges <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>: nevertheless in judgments of death the French have religiously observed at all times that nobles are beheaded, and the others hanged <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>. Some further testify that it is observed in France that if a person, however noble and illustrious he may be, commits some notable treachery and treason, he is not beheaded, but is hanged on a gibbet, and on gibbet-forks higher and more raised than the others <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>.

english.html: The crime of forgery is here patent: by the change of name and the substitution of the person, the said du Tilh having asserted that he was called, and was, Martin Guerre: for although it is lawful for everyone to change his name at his pleasure <sup class="mk" data-key="a2">a2</sup>, inasmuch as names are imposed only to recognise persons and to distinguish them one from another <sup class="mk" data-key="b2">b2</sup>: this nevertheless is understood with good faith, and without intention to defraud or injure another <sup class="mk" data-key="c2">c2</sup>. As when Pope Sergius, the second of that name, who was called in Italian Bocca di porco, that is to say Pig's Mouth, had himself named Sergius: whence since then the Pontiffs of Rome have drawn the custom of leaving, at their creation, their proper name, to take another — after the example also (as they say) of Jesus Christ, who gave the name of Peter to Simon Bar-Jona when he chose him for his disciple. <sup class="mk" data-key="d2">d2</sup> Provided therefore that the intention be not evil, one may change not only one's name, but also one's surname and arms <sup class="mk" data-key="e2">e2</sup>, and call oneself of another country: as when St Paul, in the Acts of the Apostles, called himself a citizen of Rome, although he was none <sup class="mk" data-key="f2">f2</sup>. en France, ou l'ont tient plus tenacement celle reigle
generale, que les crimes & forfaits reiettent, & aneantiſ-

d'auantage eſtre gardé en France, que ſi vne perſonne,
tant noble, & illuſtre qu'elle ſoit, commet quelque pro
dition & trahiſon notable, on ne la decole point, mais
on la pend en vn gibet, & en fourches plus hautes &
Le crime de faux eſt ici patent: par le changement
du nom, & ſuppoſition de la perſonne: ayant ledit du
Tilh aſſeuré, qu'il ſ'appeloit & eſtoit Martin Guerre:
car bien qu'il ſoit loiſible à chacun changer de nom à
ſon plaiſir {a2}, d'autant que les noms ne ſont impoſez que
pour recognoiſtre les perſonnes, & diſcerner les vnes
des autres {b2}: cela toutesfois ſ'entend auec bonne foy,
& ſans intention de frauder, ou endommager autruy {c2}.
comme quand le Pape Sergius, ſecond de ce nom, qui

vn autre à exemple auſſi (comme ils diſent) de Ieſus
